subject: pe
title: Attribution Theory
welcome_lead: Why did you win? Why did they lose? Weiner explains how we explain.
meta_desc: A-Level PE adventure on Weiner's attribution theory in sport.
final_note: Coaches who teach controllable attributions build resilient athletes.

concepts.def: Weiner's framework explaining how individuals interpret success and failure.
Stable vs unstable cause over time.
Belief that outcomes are uncontrollable, leading to passivity (Seligman).
Attributing success internally and failure externally to protect ego.

walkthroughs.body_html: Weiner's 3 × 2 model maps causes (ability, effort, task, luck) across dimensions.
Attributing failure to lack of effort (controllable, unstable) supports recovery; attributing to ability is corrosive.
Re-attribution training shifts perception of failures to controllable causes, restoring motivation.

mcqs.q: Self-serving bias is the tendency to attribute:
In attribution theory, is 'luck' an internal or external factor?
options: External - luck lies outside the performer's control.
Luck is the same thing as ability.
Crediting success to oneself (internal) but blaming failure on external factors.
Luck is the same thing as ability.

mcqs.q: What can cause learned helplessness in sport?
options: Repeatedly attributing failure to stable, internal causes such as a lack of ability.

sequence.def: Weiner's model of how we explain outcomes — the framework.
Whether causes are internal or external — first dimension.
Whether causes are stable or unstable — second dimension.
Whether causes are within our control — third dimension.
Belief that failure is unavoidable — a damaging attribution.
Crediting wins to self, blaming losses externally — protective bias.
